newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends off highs in solid volume, eyes U.S.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends off highs in solid volume, eyes U.S.

text.p: Shares ended up but off highs in solid dealings on Tuesday, as the market only momentarily drew strength from a low-inflation signal from the U.S. and investors would continue to eye U.S. data this week, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.45 percent to end at 3,011.45, trimming gains late in the session and -- at its highest -- stopping 20 points short of its all-time high of 3,041.92 set on May 6.
Brokers expected the bourse to continue slavishly to follow trends on the U.S. stock market, adding that Wall Street looked set for a breather after strong overnight gains.
"We'll be watching where the U.S. goes. After such a strong rise, there could be some profit-taking," one broker said.
Telecom share Nokia rose in lively volume, ending 4.00 markka up at 332.50 after touching 336.00 earlier in the day.

With Nokia nearing an all-time high 340.00 markka -- last hit in September 1995 before logistical problems hit profits -- some brokers saw stiff resistance, but others said the stock has shown such strength recently that technicals looked unimportant.
"Nokia has gone through so many levels lately that I don't even look at them," one broker said.

Rautaruukki added 1.50 markka to end at a new year-high of 50.50 markka in hefty 36 million markka volume, making up almost five percent of the total. Brokers said it was still attracting foreign investors after a recent offering.
Forestries outperformed, despite the weaker dollar.
UPM-Kymmene added 1.00 markka to close at 121.50 after touching 122.00 earlier. Metsa-Serla ended 1.20 markka higher at 40.20 in heavy 38 million markka volume.

Brokers said sentiment in forestries was helped by a significant drop in Norscan (North American and Scandinavian) pulp stocks: excluding Sweden, the Finnish Forest Industries Federation told Reuters they fell by 180,000 tonnes in April.
"Maybe the belief in pulp price rises is not entirely gone," one broker said. Other pointers suggest planned hikes may hold.
Cultor ended flat at 290.00 in heavy 40 million markka trade, stemming from two deals matched in-house at Merita.
Raisio extended recent losses in hefty volume, falling 16.00 markka to 384.00 markka.
"It looks like some big foreign investors have been clearing out their positions," one broker said, noting that the share had recently been highly volatile but in thin trade.

The U.S. data due for the rest of the week include price indicators -- PPI on Wednesday and CPI on Thursday. Markets are still looking for clues on what if any monetary policy moves may come from the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week.
